opening.text: Picture a big family dinner. Everyone is crowded around the table. There's noise and laughter. But one chair is empty. Maybe someone is far away. Maybe someone has passed on. You notice that chair more than any other. God sees our family tables, too. He wants every chair filled, now and forever.

mainMessage.text: God made us for families. Through the sealing power, our families can be together forever.

blocks.text: **This is His work** God's great work is to bring us home to Him. And He wants us to come in families.
For behold, this is my work and my glory—to bring to pass the immortality and eternal life of man.
Elder D. Todd Christofferson of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “The Sealing Power” from the October 2023 general conference.
Salvation is an individual matter, but exaltation is a family matter.
His work is about us, and about all of us together.
**Hearts turn toward home** Malachi taught that the hearts of children and parents would turn toward each other. That is a promise for our day.

Behold, I will send you Elijah the prophet before the coming of the great and dreadful day of the Lord: And he shall turn the heart of the fathers to the children, and the heart of the children to their fathers, lest I come and smite the earth with a curse.
Elder D. Todd Christofferson of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “The Sealing Power” from the October 2023 general conference.
With access to the sealing power, our hearts naturally turn to those who have gone before.
Love for the past is a gift.
**No chair left empty** The Lord asks us to help our family who have passed on to be with us in our eternal home.

And now, my dearly beloved brethren and sisters, let me assure you that these are principles in relation to the dead and the living that cannot be lightly passed over, as pertaining to our salvation. For their salvation is necessary and essential to our salvation, as Paul says concerning the fathers—that they without us cannot be made perfect—neither can we without our dead be made perfect.
President Henry B. Eyring, First Counselor in the First Presidency, said this in his talk “Eternal Families” from the April 2016 general conference.
The Lord also asks that we do all we can to help those of our kindred dead to be with us in our eternal home.
Every chair matters.
**Healing at the table** Some tables carry sorrow. Isaiah said the Lord binds up the brokenhearted. Temple blessings can bring that healing.

The Spirit of the Lord God is upon me; because the Lord hath anointed me to preach good tidings unto the meek; he hath sent me to bind up the brokenhearted, to proclaim liberty to the captives, and the opening of the prison to them that are bound;
Elder Dale G. Renlund of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Family History and Temple Work: Sealing and Healing” from the April 2018 general conference.
Temple blessings can heal hearts and lives and families.
He heals what hurts.
**Nothing can separate us from His love** Paul said that nothing can separate us from the love of God. That includes the hard things that happen to our families.

For I am persuaded, that neither death, nor life, nor angels, nor principalities, nor powers, nor things present, nor things to come, Nor height, nor depth, nor any other creature, shall be able to separate us from the love of God, which is in Christ Jesus our Lord.
Elder Dale G. Renlund of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Family History and Temple Work: Sealing and Healing” from the April 2018 general conference.
God, in His infinite capacity, seals and heals individuals and families despite tragedy, loss, and hardship.
His love is stronger than loss.
**Repair what is broken** Isaiah called people who help mend things "repairers of the breach." We can help mend what is broken in our families.

And they that shall be of thee shall build the old waste places: thou shalt raise up the foundations of many generations; and thou shalt be called, The repairer of the breach, The restorer of paths to dwell in.
Elder D. Todd Christofferson of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “The Sealing Power” from the October 2023 general conference.
You can add strength to your chain and perhaps even help to restore the broken links.
You can help repair.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when their family was brought closer together. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Joseph reveals himself to his brothers

blocks.text: Joseph's brothers had once sold him. Years later, he told them who he was. Then he did something surprising.

And Joseph said unto his brethren, I am Joseph; doth my father yet live? And his brethren could not answer him; for they were troubled at his presence. And Joseph said unto his brethren, Come near to me, I pray you. And they came near. And he said, I am Joseph your brother, whom ye sold into Egypt. Now therefore be not grieved, nor angry with yourselves, that ye sold me hither: for God did send me before you to preserve life.
Joseph chose to bring his family back together. Mercy made a way.

application.text: First, think of one family member you want closer. Second, reach out to them this week with a call or a note. Third, say something kind and true.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know families can be together forever. I know the Lord heals family wounds. I know Jesus Christ makes it all possible. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

opening.text: Two boats are on a lake. A storm comes. The people in the boats are afraid they'll drift apart. So someone throws a rope from one boat to the other and ties it tight. Now the boats stay together. The sealing power is that rope. It keeps families together when the waters get rough.

mainMessage.text: The sealing power ties families together, in this life and beyond. No storm can undo it when we keep our covenants.

blocks.text: **The rope was God's idea** God's work and glory is to bring us home, and He wants to bring us together.
For behold, this is my work and my glory—to bring to pass the immortality and eternal life of man.
Elder D. Todd Christofferson of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “The Sealing Power” from the October 2023 general conference.
Salvation is an individual matter, but exaltation is a family matter.
He designed it for families.
**The rope reaches back** The rope reaches to those who came before us. Their hearts turn to us, and ours turn to them.

Behold, I will send you Elijah the prophet before the coming of the great and dreadful day of the Lord: And he shall turn the heart of the fathers to the children, and the heart of the children to their fathers, lest I come and smite the earth with a curse.
Elder D. Todd Christofferson of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “The Sealing Power” from the October 2023 general conference.
With access to the sealing power, our hearts naturally turn to those who have gone before.
Hearts turn back, and the rope ties them.
**Tied to the ones who are gone** Some of our family are on the other side. The Lord asks us to help them join us in our eternal home.

And now, my dearly beloved brethren and sisters, let me assure you that these are principles in relation to the dead and the living that cannot be lightly passed over, as pertaining to our salvation. For their salvation is necessary and essential to our salvation, as Paul says concerning the fathers—that they without us cannot be made perfect—neither can we without our dead be made perfect.
President Henry B. Eyring, First Counselor in the First Presidency, said this in his talk “Eternal Families” from the April 2016 general conference.
The Lord also asks that we do all we can to help those of our kindred dead to be with us in our eternal home.
We tie the rope for them.
**Healing frayed strands** Ropes fray. Families can fray too. Isaiah said the Lord binds up the brokenhearted.

The Spirit of the Lord God is upon me; because the Lord hath anointed me to preach good tidings unto the meek; he hath sent me to bind up the brokenhearted, to proclaim liberty to the captives, and the opening of the prison to them that are bound;
Elder Dale G. Renlund of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Family History and Temple Work: Sealing and Healing” from the April 2018 general conference.
Temple blessings can heal hearts and lives and families.
He mends frayed strands.
**A rope no storm can cut** Paul said that nothing can separate us from the love of God. That love holds our families, even in hard times.

For I am persuaded, that neither death, nor life, nor angels, nor principalities, nor powers, nor things present, nor things to come, Nor height, nor depth, nor any other creature, shall be able to separate us from the love of God, which is in Christ Jesus our Lord.
Elder Dale G. Renlund of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Family History and Temple Work: Sealing and Healing” from the April 2018 general conference.
God, in His infinite capacity, seals and heals individuals and families despite tragedy, loss, and hardship.
The storm can't cut it.
**Add your hands to the rope** We can help hold and mend the rope. Our own faithful choices help our families.

And they that shall be of thee shall build the old waste places: thou shalt raise up the foundations of many generations; and thou shalt be called, The repairer of the breach, The restorer of paths to dwell in.
Elder D. Todd Christofferson of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “The Sealing Power” from the October 2023 general conference.
You can add strength to your chain and perhaps even help to restore the broken links.
Your hands make the rope stronger.

story.title: Joseph and Jacob meet again

blocks.text: Joseph and his father had been apart for many years. When they finally met, there were few words.

And Joseph made ready his chariot, and went up to meet Israel his father, to Goshen, and presented himself unto him; and he fell on his neck, and wept on his neck a good while. And Israel said unto Joseph, Now let me die, since I have seen thy face, because thou art yet alive.
They held on and wept. Their love had held through the years. Family love can do that.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when someone welcomed them home. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: The father runs to his son

blocks.text: A young man left home and wasted what he had. When he came back, he expected anger. He found something else.
And he arose, and came to his father. But when he was yet a great way off, his father saw him, and had compassion, and ran, and fell on his neck, and kissed him.
The father had been watching the road. That is how God feels about our families. He is watching, and He is ready to run.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when they wanted someone they love to share something good. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Lehi wants his family to partake

blocks.text: Lehi tasted the fruit of the tree of life. It was sweet beyond anything he knew. His first thought was not of himself.

And as I partook of the fruit thereof it filled my soul with exceedingly great joy; wherefore, I began to be desirous that my family should partake of it also; for I knew that it was desirable above all other fruit.
When we find something good, we want our family to have it too. That desire is part of the gospel.

application.text: First, think of one good thing the gospel has given you. Second, share it with a family member in a simple way. Third, invite them with no pressure.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know God gathers His children. I know no family is too far gone for His love. I know Jesus Christ is the Good Shepherd. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

opening.text: A cup falls and breaks. You could throw it out. Or you could glue it back, piece by piece. When you're done, it holds water again. You can still see the lines. But it works, and it's more precious now than before. Families can be like that cup. Broken at times, and made whole again by God.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when they forgave or were forgiven in their family. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Joseph comforts his brothers

blocks.text: Joseph's father had died. His brothers feared he would now punish them. Joseph chose another way.

But as for you, ye thought evil against me; but God meant it unto good, to bring to pass, as it is this day, to save much people alive. Now therefore fear ye not: I will nourish you, and your little ones. And he comforted them, and spake kindly unto them.
Joseph could have held on to the hurt. Instead he spoke kindly. That is how a family gets mended.

application.text: First, think of a hurt in your family that still lingers. Second, decide what small step toward peace you can take. Third, take it this week, and leave the rest to God.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know God can mend what is broken. I know families can heal and be sealed forever. I know Jesus Christ is the Healer. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.
